adaptive_generation.description: Guidelines for adaptive SOW generation based on user input analysis

content_requirements.description: Guidelines for defining content in POC
rules: Business relevance must be clearly stated (e.g., textbook, policy document, training manual)
Technical format must be specified (PDF, HTML, PNG scans, etc.)
Volume of content in business terms (pages, books) and technical terms (GiB, zipped files)
Access control - define who loads content and who reads/consumes it
Volume of access - average over time (day, month), simultaneous logins
Adapt content requirements based on industry context and complexity level

requirement_specificity.description: Requirements must be specific and measurable
requirement_specificity.good_example: The solution should extract names, dates, locations and acronyms related to financial domain from documents
requirement_specificity.bad_example: The solution should be capable of extracting relevant information from documents
rules: Avoid vague statements
Use concrete examples
Define specific domains and constraints
Specify what is in-scope and out-of-scope
Tailor specificity to project complexity level
Include industry-specific requirements and constraints

accuracy_metrics.description: Accuracy must be quantified and measurable
rules: Quantify accuracy targets based on complexity: Simple (85%+), Moderate (90%+), Complex (95%+), Enterprise (99%+)
Define measurement method (human review, BLEU, ROUGE, etc.)
Call out constraints - language limits (e.g., English only), domain constraints
Set realistic expectations for POC vs Production
Include industry-specific accuracy requirements
Align metrics with identified business drivers

scope_definition.description: Clear distinction between POC and Production scope
rules: Document must exclusively describe POC scope OR clearly separate POC from Production deliverables
Explicitly list out-of-scope items based on complexity level
Define what will be delivered in POC phase
Clarify what requires future phases or change requests
Include industry-specific scope considerations
Align scope with assessed project complexity and user constraints
Clearly justify choice of specific LLM (e.g., Claude, Nova, Titan)
Prefer AWS Bedrock models when available
If using non-Bedrock LLM, provide additional justification
Justify vector database choice (OpenSearch, Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector, etc.)
If not using AWS managed vector DB, explain why
Note: POC quality should not be compromised for Bedrock availability
Consider industry-specific AI service requirements
Scale AI service selection based on project complexity
Use S3 Intelligent Tiering for cost savings
Define DynamoDB data retention policies based on complexity (Simple: 7 days, Moderate: 30 days, Complex: 90 days, Enterprise: 1 year)
Implement lifecycle policies for temporary data
Use appropriate storage classes based on access patterns
Consider industry-specific data retention requirements
Scale storage solutions based on project complexity and data volume
Must call out deployment region(s)
Must show if solution spans multiple AWS accounts (for complex/enterprise projects)
Include ancillary services: IAM, ECR, WAF, KMS, CloudWatch, CloudTrail
Show VPC and Availability Zones when using compute (EC2, ECS, EKS)
Clearly show data flow and component interactions
Include industry-specific security and compliance components
Scale architecture complexity based on project assessment
Specify if testing is manual or automated based on complexity level
Describe testing process in detail
Define test data requirements
Specify number of reviewers and their roles based on project complexity
Set realistic success criteria with percentages aligned to complexity level
Include industry-specific testing requirements (e.g., clinical validation for healthcare)
Scale testing rigor based on project complexity and business criticality
Prefer AWS Lambda or Step Functions for API hosting
Avoid EC2-based hosting unless justified
If EC2 required, use Spot instances and Graviton processors to reduce cost
Consider serverless-first architecture
Scale hosting approach based on complexity: Simple (Lambda), Moderate (Lambda + API Gateway), Complex (ECS/EKS), Enterprise (Multi-service architecture)
Include industry-specific hosting considerations (e.g., compliance requirements)

Verify regional availability of chosen model

Consider model capabilities vs. requirements

Describe usage per persona (view, upload, approve)
Capture concurrency requirements based on complexity level
Define access control per persona
Include industry-specific personas and usage patterns
